name: showreel-c3-liberty-green

voice.text: Why is the Statue of Liberty green? In 1886, she was the colour of a shiny new coin. Her skin is copper, thinner than 3 millimetres. Year after year, air and sea salt reacted with the copper. In about 20 years, she turned completely green. In 1906, there was a plan to paint her. People protested, and her outside was never painted. Turns out, that green layer protects the copper underneath. The green is her armour.

caption:
She wasn't built green. The Statue of Liberty was shiny copper-brown in 1886, and that green coat is what keeps her standing. 🗽

Save this for your next trip to New York. Which landmark should we explain next? 👇
